title: Clinical Protocol for Assessing PONV in Cesarean Patients
author: Gabriel Magalhães Nunes Guimarães
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.q9ndz5e

steps.title: Screen Patients for Inclusion
steps.instruction: Verify that patients waiting for cesarean section meet both necessary inclusion criteria.

substeps.instruction: Increment the 'not included' counter for patients failing either criterion.

steps.title: Obtain Informed Consent
steps.instruction: Execute the informed consent protocol using two copies of the specific written informed consent (tcle.doc).

substeps.instruction: Ensure both the principal investigator and participant sign both copies.
Store one copy with the principal investigator and provide the other to the participant.

steps.title: Collect Baseline Patient Data
steps.instruction: Gather patient history and demographics and record them in the online electronic data capture form.

substeps.instruction: Record nausea in the first trimester (true/false).
Record nausea in the third trimester (true/false).

steps.title: Record Post-Cesarean Clinical Data
steps.instruction: Acquire and store the following data in the online electronic data capture form after the cesarean ends.

substeps.instruction: Verify spinal anesthesia only (true/false); if false, exclude the patient.
Record doses for hyperbaric bupivacaine, spinal sufentanil, spinal fentanyl, and spinal morphine.
Record basal mean arterial pressure (MAP) and minimum MAP after spinal before birth.
Record intraoperative ondansetron dose and dexamethasone dose.

steps.title: Assess PONV During First Two Hours
steps.instruction: Monitor and record PONV data in the PACU during the first two postoperative hours in the electronic data capture form.

substeps.instruction: Rate nausea intensity on a scale of 0-10.

steps.title: Assess PONV Between 2 and 24 Hours
steps.instruction: Query the patient regarding PONV between 2 and 24 hours after the cesarean and record in the electronic data capture form.

substeps.instruction: Rate nausea intensity on a scale of 0-10.
